thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: prod-kv-cache continuous-batcher spike detected on prod-shard-7. Error rate 504s=4.8% (baseline 0.2%). Latency p95 increased from 120ms -> 1.6s. Suspected cause: large structured tool-call responses causing batch breaks and KV cache blowup. Alert id: ALERT-20260315-001 :rotating_light: 

alice_oncall: Acked. I'm on it. Can folks drop current symptoms + customer impact here?

bob_sre: Seeing sustained batch queue length growth across runtime-replicas 7a-7d. Continuous-batcher is assembling very skewed batches (1 large request + many small). GPU memory pressure up ~22% on those hosts and KV cache eviction rate jumped. Logs show repeated prefix misses for similar request keys.

charlie_ml: Correlating with model telemetry — a recent customer workload started returning chunked structured outputs (tool calls that return big JSON arrays of search results). Those structured outputs are large (~6-15KB) and contain many repeated keys, which pushes tokenization past our prefix-cache-length heuristics and invalidates cached KV entries mid-batch. Essentially a lot of cache entries become unshared, so batch becomes ineffective and per-token costs spike.

alice_oncall: Which customers are impacted?

eric_support: Support queue: two distinct customers (org-redraft, org-scribebox) reported intermittent 504s for generation endpoints starting ~00:17 UTC. Both on Dedicated pools pinned to prod-shard-7. Low volume but high severity for their SLAs. Marked as P1 because it's causing user-facing errors.

bob_sre: Quick metrics: error spikes at 00:18 UTC, sustained until now. p95 latency hit 1.6s; p99 ~3.2s. Continuous_batch.success_ratio dropped from 99.6% -> 93.1%. KV cache eviction rate increased ~8x.

dana_runtime: Hypothesis: tool/function-calls returning large structured payloads are crossing `continuous_batch.max_prefix_tokens` and causing per-request rerouting to single-request batches. That creates lots of tiny KV entries and thrashes the cache. Also our `kv_cache.eviction_policy` on these shards favors LRU which gets overwhelmed because keys have high cardinality (each structured output contains unique IDs).

frank_ops: Any quick mitigations we can flip without code deploy? Something via runtime config roll?

alice_oncall: Prioritize quick customer relief. Options: 1) Temporarily route affected routes to a smaller model variant or lower batch concurrency; 2) Apply a config to treat structured tool-call outputs as bypass for batching (i.e., force single-request execution) — but that may increase latency per call; 3) Short-term: drop structured output parsing for the route so responses are plain text (reduces tokens). Which is fastest?

charlie_ml: Fastest low-risk: per-route config to cap `continuous_batch.max_output_tokens` and enforce `structured_output.max_size_bytes=4096` (truncate/inline). We have an API that can push a config override to the Dedicated pool control plane. That will reduce the large outputs hitting batch heuristics.

bob_sre: I can push a targeted runtime override to prod-shard-7 for routes matching `/v1/generate` where header `x-customer-org` in [org-redraft, org-scribebox]. It will set `continuous_batch.max_output_tokens=512` and `structured_output.max_size_bytes=4096`. Doing this now will likely reduce cache fragmentation.

alice_oncall: Go for it. Add a short note in the thread when done. Also prepare rollback steps.

bob_sre: Executing quick patch via control-plane API now. Command: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "target": "prod-shard-7",
    "match": {"path": "/v1/generate", "header.x-customer-org": ["org-redraft","org-scribebox"]},
    "overrides": {"continuous_batch.max_output_tokens": 512, "structured_output.max_size_bytes": 4096}
  }'
```

incident-bot: CONFIG-APPLY: override request received (id cfg-20260315-77). Rollout started to prod-shard-7 replicas.

bob_sre: Patch applied to 7a/7b/7c now, rolling to 7d. Watching metrics.

dana_runtime: After the patch I see immediate reduction in average batch size variance; batch sharing ratio up ~18% within 60s. KV cache eviction rate falling back toward baseline. Nice.

eric_support: org-redraft reports reduced errors; their last failure was 00:23 UTC. Scribebox still seeing a few 504s but trending down. I'll send a quick heads-up to both customers noting we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA.

alice_oncall: Good. Keep the override for 2 hours while we validate. Create a canary to test broader impact before expanding. Also collect example requests that triggered big structured outputs for ML/Runtime to analyze.

charlie_ml: Pulling sample traces now. The problematic pattern: tool calls that return variable-length search hits arrays with embedded document snippets. We should implement server-side compression for tool outputs and a structured-output sanitizer that collapses long arrays when used in production. Postmortem item.

frank_ops: I'll prepare the rollback plan: to remove override run: ```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime/overrides/cfg-20260315-77" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN"
``` Rollback safe window 10 minutes; we should monitor before delete.

alice_oncall: Handoff: I'm oncall until 01:00 UTC; @frank_ops will take over active watch if this persists beyond. @postmortem-bot please create incident tracker with tags: kvcache, continuous-batching, toolcall-structout and link this thread.

postmortem-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-47. Assigning to alice_oncall for initial timeline and charlie_ml for root-cause analysis.

alice_oncall: Thanks everyone. Summary for now: mitigation applied (per-route structured output cap), metrics improving, customers notified, postmortem created. Next steps: collect request/response examples, propose long-term fixes (structured-output size-limits, KV key normalization, smarter batching policy), and schedule postmortem. I'll update when handing over to frank_ops at 00:55 UTC. :white_check_mark:
